title: POC Weekly - Redwood Private VPC Pilot Sync
summary: Weekly check-in for Redwood Private VPC pilot. Main focus: networking routing issues observed during staging load tests, upcoming kernel/driver upgrade on on-prem nodes, KMS integration for model encryption, and next steps for canary rollout. Action items assigned for logs, test plan, and scheduling upgrade window.
topics: throughput / latency results from last run
canary rollout plan and rollback criteria
action_items: Priya Singh - share VPC flow logs and traceroute outputs for the affected subnets by 2026-11-06
Diego Ramos (SE) - prepare step-by-step upgrade runbook for node kernel and NV driver update, include rollback steps, due 2026-11-09
Maya Patel (AE) - share pricing impact for dedicated nodes post-upgrade and options for reserved capacity by 2026-11-07
Mark O'Connor - provide SOC2 evidence location and confirm KMS key rotation policy by 2026-11-10
next_steps: Run staged kernel/driver upgrade in staging cluster on 2026-11-08
Collect detailed perf logs during a 2-hour load test (Diego to trigger) on 2026-11-09
Redwood to share updated security whitepaper and KMS integration notes (Maya)
Schedule follow-up post-upgrade sync for 2026-11-11 at 10:00 AM PT
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining the weekly sync. Quick roll call, um, Redwood on the line - Diego and me, Maya.
[00:10] James Li: Hey all, James here.
[00:12] Priya Singh: Priya on infra.
[00:14] Mark O'Connor: Mark from security.
[00:18] Maya Patel: Cool. Agenda - network/routing follow-up from last week's staging run, the kernel/driver upgrade plan for on-prem nodes, KMS questions, and then canary rollout criteria.
[00:32] Diego Ramos: I'll start with the perf numbers we saw. During the last run we saw about a 15% tail-latency increase on long sequences when workers hit a GC pause after NV driver churn, so p50 was fine but p95/p99 spiked. Some of that correlates to multiple nodes hitting a slow path when they lost connectivity to the object store for model shards.
[00:55] Sofia Martinez: Yeah we noticed some timeouts to the S3 gateway, and the fallback to local shard didn't always complete fast enough.
[01:05] Priya Singh: On our side we saw asymmetric routing in one of the subnets, traceroutes show traffic leaving via the NAT but returning on a different AZ route, so TCP reordering might be causing retransmits.
[01:18] Maya Patel: That matches the VPC flow logs Diego asked for. Priya, did you capture the flows for the times Diego referenced?
[01:25] Priya Singh: I have flow logs, but I haven't correlated timestamps yet; I'll upload the raw logs to the shared folder and add a short note, target is Friday.
[01:33] Mark O'Connor: Also, we noticed when the node reboots there are ephemeral keys cached in memory for the KV cache; we need to confirm Redwood's recommended key rotation and the behavior with KMS after a reboot.
[01:44] Diego Ramos: Right - by default Redwood Private will rehydrate KV cache and we recommend rotating session keys at the controller level. For the KMS integration, we support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS and HSM connectors on-prem, but the agent version you run needs the new KMS client for keywrap v2.
[01:59] Priya Singh: Hmm which agent version includes that? Our appliance is running agent 1.12.1.
[02:05] Diego Ramos: The KMS client update is in 1.14.x, and also the kernel driver update we want to push includes NV driver 525.x which resolves a disconnect bug we saw.
[02:15] James Li: So we need to schedule both agent and kernel/driver upgrades - any order dependency?
[02:20] Diego Ramos: We recommend kernel/driver first, reboot nodes, verify device stability, then roll agent update. The main reason is driver-level fixes reduce connection churn; agent update depends on driver stability for the enhanced KMS client.
[02:33] Maya Patel: We'll put an upgrade runbook together. Diego, can you create the step-by-step and list the exact package names?
[02:38] Diego Ramos: Yep. I'll include checksums, commands to drain workloads, canary percentage, and a rollback plan.
[02:44] Priya Singh: For rollback, what's the expected behavior? Will models revert to hosted Redwood endpoints or remain offline?
[02:50] Diego Ramos: Good question - we support automatic fallback routing to the Redwood-hosted API if you opt-in and if network policy allows egress. For this pilot you have egress blocked by default, so we recommend enabling controlled egress for the canary window or testing a subset of requests only.
[03:05] James Li: Egress to hosted is sensitive for us, we need to keep PHI in-house.
[03:09] Mark O'Connor: Yes, security policy prevents sending PHI externally. We'll need a strict allowlist and audit trailing.
[03:16] Maya Patel: Understood — for PHI workloads we can keep everything on-prem. For non-PHI test traffic we can enable egress to speed rollback if needed.
[03:25] Sofia Martinez: Quick perf question - after the driver update should we expect a raw throughput change or just improved stability under long sequences?
[03:33] Diego Ramos: Mostly stability and lower tail latency. There is a minor throughput improvement for batch sizes > 8 due to better kernel memory handling, maybe 5-8% on our internal tests. Real gains for you will be lower error/retry rate which reduces effective latency.
[03:48] Priya Singh: About the asymmetric routing - we can change the route tables but want to be sure that's the real cause. We'll share traceroutes and flow logs; Diego, can you correlate once you have them?
[03:58] Diego Ramos: Yup, send them to me and I'll correlate with the perf logs.
[04:02] James Li: Action on our side - Priya will push logs; Mark will check policy for limited egress for canary; Sofia will prepare a test set with non-PHI examples.
[04:12] Maya Patel: Pricing note - if you need reserved capacity after upgrade we can model committed nodes; I'll send the updated estimate.
[04:17] James Li: Great, that helps budgeting.
[04:20] Mark O'Connor: One security ask - can you confirm audit log retention and where logs are stored for the on-prem control plane? We need to include that in the compliance pack.
[04:29] Diego Ramos: Audit logs are written to the local audit collector and can be forwarded to your SIEM (we've tested Splunk and Elastic). Retention is configurable; by default the control plane keeps 90 days but you can extend. I'll document the exact paths and config flags.
[04:42] Priya Singh: Also, what about rolling back ML model versions if the canary shows quality regressions? Do you have an automated snapshot/rollback?
[04:50] Diego Ramos: We have model version pinning and rollback via the deployment controller. We snapshot the model config and KV cache—rollback is a config change and a graceful restart. There is some warm-up cost for cache misses, we can quantify that in the runbook.
[04:59] Maya Patel: Okay let's recap: Priya share logs by 11/6; Diego produce upgrade runbook by 11/9 and run the staging upgrade 11/8; Maya share pricing and security docs by 11/7; Mark confirm limited egress policy and SOC2 evidence by 11/10; follow-up sync 11/11. Anything else?
[05:18] James Li: Nothing from me. Thanks folks.
[05:20] Maya Patel: Thanks all, we'll send meeting notes and the runbook links after the call. Appreciate it.
[05:25] [Meeting ends]
